body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_W\), \(P\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n})<m_{\Sigma}/2\}=O(n^{-2})\). On the complementary event, \(\|R_n(\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n})-\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq4n^{-2}/m_{\Sigma}^2\); consequently the ridge-totalized reduced forms, score, estimated influence process, and multiplier critical value differ from their inverse-defined versions by \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Thus the near-singular fallback event is asymptotically immaterial for every stated weak limit and, because confidence sets lie in compact \(K\), for the stated expected outer-loss rates.
body.justification: The lemma makes all reported procedures measurable on singular samples while preserving their first-order contact and interior behavior.
body.gap: Watson et al.'s implementation removes undefined rows; this result replaces that implicit conditioning by an every-sample convention and quantifies its uniform asymptotic cost.
body.consumer: Software can return an interval or confidence hull on every dataset without altering the endpoint laws, coverage claim, or adaptive loss frontier.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(A=\Sigma_{zz}(P)\), \(\widehat A_n=\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n}\), and \(\rho_n=n^{-2}\).  All constants below may depend on the fixed dimension \(d\), the compact interval \(K\), and the constants defining \(\mathcal P_W\), but not on \(P\in\mathcal P_W\) or \(n\).

\textbf{1. A fourth-moment covariance bound.}
Because \(A\) is a principal submatrix of \(\Sigma(P)\), assumption \(\mathrm{ass:covariance\mbox{-}conditioning}\) and the variational characterization of the smallest eigenvalue give
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(A)\geq m_{\Sigma}.
\]
Let \(A_n^0=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n Z_iZ_i^{\prime}\) and \(\overline Z_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i\).  The centering convention in the definition of \(\widehat\Sigma_n\) gives
\[
 \widehat A_n=A_n^0-\overline Z_n\overline Z_n^{\prime}.
\]
For fixed coordinates \(j,k\), put \(U_i^{jk}=Z_{ij}Z_{ik}-E_P[Z_{ij}Z_{ik}]\).  By Cauchy--Schwarz and assumption \(\mathrm{ass:eighth\mbox{-}moment}\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_W}E_P|U_i^{jk}|^4<\infty.
\]
Independence and centering imply, by expanding the fourth power and retaining only index patterns in which every index occurs at least twice,
\[
 E_P\left|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nU_i^{jk}\right|^4
 =n^{-4}\left\{nE_P[(U_1^{jk})^4]+3n(n-1)E_P[(U_1^{jk})^2]^2\right\}
 \leq Cn^{-2}.
\]
Since \(d\) is fixed, equivalence of matrix norms therefore yields
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_W}E_P\|A_n^0-A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^4\leq Cn^{-2}. \tag{1}
\]
Similarly, expansion of the eighth power of each coordinate of \(\overline Z_n\) has at most four distinct indices in every nonzero term: any index occurring exactly once makes that term vanish by assumption \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}centered}\).  H\"older's inequality and the uniform eighth-moment bound thus give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_W}E_P\|\overline Z_n\|_2^8\leq Cn^{-4}. \tag{2}
\]
Using \(\|vv^{\prime}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|v\|_2^2\), equations \((1)\)--\((2)\), and \((a+b)^4\leq8(a^4+b^4)\), we obtain
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_W}E_P\|\widehat A_n-A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^4\leq Cn^{-2}. \tag{3}
\]
For symmetric matrices, the variational formula gives directly
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat A_n)
 \geq \lambda_{\min}(A)-\|\widehat A_n-A\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Consequently, Markov's inequality and \((3)\) imply
\[
 \begin{split}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_W}P\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat A_n)<m_{\Sigma}/2\}
 &\leq \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_W}P\{\|\widehat A_n-A\|_{\mathrm{op}}>m_{\Sigma}/2\}\\
 &\leq (2/m_{\Sigma})^4\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_W}E_P\|\widehat A_n-A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^4
 \leq Cn^{-2}. \tag{4}
 \end{split}
\]
This proves the asserted uniform probability bound.

\textbf{2. Resolvent and smooth-score comparisons.}
Let \(E_n=\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat A_n)\geq m_{\Sigma}/2\}\).  On \(E_n\), both \(T_0=\widehat A_n^{-1}\) and \(T_{\rho}=(\widehat A_n+\rho_n I_d)^{-1}\) exist, and
\[
 \|T_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq 2/m_{\Sigma},
 \qquad
 \|T_{\rho}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq 2/m_{\Sigma}.
\]
The resolvent identity, proved by multiplying both sides by \(\widehat A_n+\rho_n I_d\) and \(\widehat A_n\), is
\[
 T_{\rho}-T_0=-\rho_nT_{\rho}T_0.
\]
It follows that, on \(E_n\),
\[
 \|R_n(\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n})-\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq \frac{4n^{-2}}{m_{\Sigma}^2}. \tag{5}
\]

We next make the comparison with the inverse-defined objects explicit.  For a generic covariance matrix \(S\), write \(A_S=S_{zz}\), \(b_{x,S}=S_{zx}\), \(b_{y,S}=S_{zy}\),
\[
 b_{\theta,S}=b_{y,S}-\theta b_{x,S},\qquad
 T_{r,S}=(A_S+rI_d)^{-1},\qquad
 u_{r,S}(\theta)=T_{r,S}b_{\theta,S},
\]
and
\[
 f_{r,S}(\theta)=\|u_{r,S}(\theta)\|_2^2-\tau^2.
\]
Thus, at \(S=\widehat\Sigma_n\), the choice \(r=\rho_n\) gives the ridge-defined reduced forms and score, whereas \(r=0\) gives their inverse-defined versions on \(E_n\).  Since \(K\) is compact, \(M_K=\sup_{\theta\in K}|\theta|<\infty\).  The eighth-moment assumption implies uniformly that
\[
 \|\widehat\Sigma_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(1). \tag{6}
\]
Indeed, the square of its operator norm is bounded, up to a fixed-dimensional constant, by a sample average of \(\|W_i\|_2^4\) plus \(\|\overline W_n\|_2^4\), whose expectations are uniformly bounded.

Equations \((5)\)--\((6)\) now give
\[
 \|\widehat\beta_n-\widetilde\beta_n\|_2
 +\|\widehat\alpha_n-\widetilde\alpha_n\|_2
 =O_P(n^{-2}) \tag{7}
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal P_W\), where tildes denote inverse-defined versions on \(E_n\), with any measurable extension on \(E_n^c\).  The identity
\[
 |\|x\|_2^2-\|y\|_2^2|
 \leq (\|x\|_2+\|y\|_2)\|x-y\|_2
\]
and \((6)\)--\((7)\) then yield
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in K}|\widehat q_n(\theta)-\widetilde q_n(\theta)|=O_P(n^{-2}). \tag{8}
\]

For completeness, the derivative comparison needed for the influence process follows from a direct differentiation, rather than from an unstated smoothness assertion.  For a symmetric perturbation \(H\), set \(h_\theta=H_{zy}-\theta H_{zx}\).  Differentiating the inverse identity gives \(D T_{r,S}[H]=-T_{r,S}H_{zz}T_{r,S}\), and hence
\[
 D_Sf_{r,S}(\theta)[H]
 =2u_{r,S}(\theta)^{\prime}T_{r,S}
   \{h_\theta-H_{zz}u_{r,S}(\theta)\}. \tag{9}
\]
On \(E_n\cap\{\|\widehat\Sigma_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq M\}\), formula \((9)\), the resolvent identity, and the triangle inequality imply for a constant \(C_M<\infty\)
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in K}
 \|D_Sf_{\rho_n,\widehat\Sigma_n}(\theta)
      -D_Sf_{0,\widehat\Sigma_n}(\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq C_Mn^{-2}. \tag{10}
\]
No division beyond the inverses controlled in \((5)\) occurs in this step.

Put
\[
 H_{i,n}=(W_i-\overline W_n)(W_i-\overline W_n)^{\prime}-\widehat\Sigma_n.
\]
The fourth-moment consequence of assumption \(\mathrm{ass:eighth\mbox{-}moment}\) gives
\[
 n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\|H_{i,n}\|_{\mathrm F}^2=O_P(1) \tag{11}
\]
uniformly.  Applying \((10)\) to \(H_{i,n}\), then using \((6)\) and \((11)\), proves
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in K}
 \left[n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n
   \{\widehat\psi_i(\theta)-\widetilde\psi_i(\theta)\}^2
 \right]^{1/2}
 =O_P(n^{-2})=o_P(n^{-1/2}). \tag{12}
\]
The reverse triangle inequality for Euclidean norms also gives
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in K}|\widehat\sigma_n(\theta)-\widetilde\sigma_n(\theta)|
 \leq
 \sup_{\theta\in K}
 \left[n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n
   \{\widehat\psi_i(\theta)-\widetilde\psi_i(\theta)\}^2
 \right]^{1/2}
 =O_P(n^{-2}). \tag{13}
\]

We record why studentization is uniformly safe.  Formula \((9)\) shows that, as a function of \(\theta\), each inverse-defined influence score is a polynomial of degree at most two.  Its squared value is therefore a polynomial of degree at most four.  The finitely many empirical coefficients of these polynomials are continuous functions of \(\widehat\Sigma_n\) and sample averages of products of at most four coordinates of \(W_i\).  Their variances are uniformly bounded by assumption \(\mathrm{ass:eighth\mbox{-}moment}\).  Entrywise Chebyshev bounds, \((3)\), and compactness of \(K\) consequently imply
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in K}|\widetilde\sigma_n(\theta)-\sigma_P(\theta)|=o_P(1) \tag{14}
\]
uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_W\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:score\mbox{-}nondegeneracy}\), \((13)\), and \((14)\) imply that, with probability tending to one uniformly,
\[
 \inf_{\theta\in K}\{\widehat\sigma_n(\theta)\wedge\widetilde\sigma_n(\theta)\}
 \geq c_{\sigma}/2. \tag{15}
\]
Thus the truncation by \(n^{-1}\) in both critical-value formulas is inactive for all sufficiently large \(n\) on this event.

\textbf{3. Stability of the conditional Gaussian quantile.}
Let
\[
 v_r(\theta)=\bigl(D_Sf_{r,\widehat\Sigma_n}(\theta)[H_{1,n}],\ldots,
 D_Sf_{r,\widehat\Sigma_n}(\theta)[H_{n,n}]\bigr)^{\prime},
 \qquad
 a_r(\theta)=\frac{v_r(\theta)}{\|v_r(\theta)\|_2}.
\]
On the event in \((15)\), these vectors are well defined for \(r\in\{0,\rho_n\}\), and
\[
 \frac{n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_iD_Sf_{r,\widehat\Sigma_n}(\theta)[H_{i,n}]}
 {(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nD_Sf_{r,\widehat\Sigma_n}(\theta)[H_{i,n}]^2)^{1/2}}
 =\xi^{\prime}a_r(\theta). \tag{16}
\]
Equations \((12)\)--\((15)\) and the elementary normalization inequality
\[
 \left\|\frac{x}{\|x\|_2}-\frac{y}{\|y\|_2}\right\|_2
 \leq \frac{2\|x-y\|_2}{\|y\|_2}
\]
give
\[
 e_n:=\sup_{\theta\in K}\|a_{\rho_n}(\theta)-a_0(\theta)\|_2=O_P(n^{-2}) \tag{17}
\]
uniformly.  By \((9)\), \(v_r(\theta)\) is a vector-valued polynomial of degree at most two.  Hence all vectors in
\[
 \mathcal A_r=\{a_r(\theta):\theta\in K\}
\]
belong to a subspace of dimension at most three, and \(\mathcal A_0\cup\mathcal A_{\rho_n}\) belongs to a subspace of dimension at most six.  Conditional on the data, the two suprema in the critical values are therefore support functions of compact subsets of the unit sphere evaluated at one standard Gaussian vector \(G\in\mathbb R^r\), where \(1\leq r\leq6\).

We now prove the needed quantile continuity in this fixed dimension.  Fix \(p=1-\eta>1/2\).  For a nonempty compact \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb S^{r-1}\), let
\[
 X_{\mathcal A}=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}a^{\prime}G.
\]
For any \(a_0\in\mathcal A\),
\[
 a_0^{\prime}G\leq X_{\mathcal A}\leq\|G\|_2,
\]
so its \(p\)-quantile lies between \(z_p=\Phi^{-1}(p)>0\) and the \(p\)-quantile of \(\|N(0,I_6)\|_2\).  Write \(G=RU\), where \(R=\|G\|_2\) and \(U\) is uniform on the unit sphere and independent of \(R\).  On the spherical cap \(\{a_0^{\prime}U\geq1/2\}\), whose probability is bounded below uniformly over \(1\leq r\leq6\),
\[
 1/2\leq \sup_{a\in\mathcal A}a^{\prime}U\leq1.
\]
The radial density is continuous and bounded below on every compact subinterval of \((0,\infty)\).  Conditioning on this cap therefore proves that constants \(c_p>0\) and \(s_p>0\), depending only on \(p\) and the bound \(r\leq6\), satisfy
\[
 P\{x<X_{\mathcal A}\leq x+s\}\geq c_ps \tag{18}
\]
whenever \(0<s\leq s_p\) and \(x\) lies in a fixed compact interval containing every such \(p\)-quantile.  The same polar representation shows that \(X_{\mathcal A}\) has no atom at a positive point.

If compact \(\mathcal A,\mathcal B\subseteq\mathbb S^{r-1}\) have Euclidean Hausdorff distance at most \(e\), then
\[
 |X_{\mathcal A}-X_{\mathcal B}|\leq e\|G\|_2. \tag{19}
\]
For sufficiently small \(e\), choose \(u_e=C e\sqrt{\log(1/e)}\), with \(C\) large enough that
\[
 P\{e\|G\|_2>u_e\}\leq e^2
\]
uniformly for \(r\leq6\).  Apply \((18)\) at the \(p\)-quantile of \(X_{\mathcal B}\), with \(s=2e^2/c_p\), and use \((19)\).  This gives
\[
 Q_p(X_{\mathcal A})\leq Q_p(X_{\mathcal B})+u_e+2e^2/c_p.
\]
Interchanging \(\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal B\) proves
\[
 |Q_p(X_{\mathcal A})-Q_p(X_{\mathcal B})|
 \leq C_p e\sqrt{\log(1/e)}. \tag{20}
\]
Thus \((16)\)--\((17)\) and \((20)\) yield
\[
 |\widehat c_{1-\eta}-\widetilde c_{1-\eta}|
 =O_P(n^{-2}\sqrt{\log n})=o_P(n^{-1/2}) \tag{21}
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal P_W\).  This derivation also shows, under the same coupling of multipliers,
\[
 E_{\xi}\left[
 \sup_{\theta\in K}|\xi^{\prime}a_{\rho_n}(\theta)-\xi^{\prime}a_0(\theta)|
 \mathrel{\big|}W_1,\ldots,W_n\right]
 \leq \sqrt6\,e_n=O_P(n^{-2}),
\]
which is the asserted first-order equivalence of the standardized multiplier influence processes.

The same covariance argument applies conditionally to an empirical-bootstrap resample.  Conditional on the data, its eighth-moment envelope is \(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\|W_i\|_2^8=O_P(1)\).  Repeating the fourth-moment expansion conditionally shows, on \(E_n\), that the conditional probability that the resample instrument covariance is more than \(m_{\Sigma}/4\) away from \(\widehat A_n\) is \(O_P(n^{-2})\).  On the complementary conditional event its smallest eigenvalue is at least \(m_{\Sigma}/4\), and the preceding resolvent and derivative calculations apply with changed constants.  Hence ridge totalization is also asymptotically immaterial for the empirical-bootstrap weak limits.

Equations \((7)\), \((8)\), \((12)\), and \((21)\), together with \((4)\), establish the claimed uniform \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) equivalence.  For the positive-part endpoint maps, the only nonsmooth operation additionally satisfies
\[
 |\sqrt{x_+}-\sqrt{y_+}|\leq\sqrt{|x-y|},
\]
so the \(O_P(n^{-2})\) score perturbation contributes only \(O_P(n^{-1})\) at quadratic contact, which is negligible after \(n^{1/4}\) scaling; away from contact the ordinary Lipschitz bound is even sharper.  Thus all stated contact and interior weak limits are unchanged.

\textbf{4. Expected-loss contribution of the fallback event.}
The target set is nonempty under the structural restrictions.  Indeed, assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:outcome\mbox{-}equation}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:outcome\mbox{-}orthogonality}\) give
\[
 \Sigma_{zy}(P)=\Sigma_{zz}(P)\gamma+\theta_0\Sigma_{zx}(P),
 \qquad
 \alpha(P)=\gamma+\theta_0\beta(P).
\]
Because \(\theta_0\in K\) and assumption \(\mathrm{ass:l2\mbox{-}leakage}\) gives \(\|\gamma\|_2\leq\tau\),
\[
 q_P(\theta_0)=\|\gamma\|_2^2-\tau^2\leq0,
 \qquad
 \theta_0\in\Theta_I(P).
\]
Let \(D_K=\operatorname{diam}(K)<\infty\).  For every closed \(A\subseteq K\), including \(A=\varnothing\), the definition of the directed loss and nonemptiness of \(\Theta_I(P)\) imply
\[
 0\leq d_{\to}(A,\Theta_I(P))\leq D_K.
\]
Therefore the contribution of the near-singular event to any stated expected outer-loss bound is at most
\[
 D_KP(E_n^c)=O(n^{-2}),
\]
uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_W\).  This is negligible relative to both \(n^{-1/4}\) and \(n^{-1/2}\), completing the proof.
